summary: Milestone 2026.04.99 closeout was short and mostly orchestration-bound: the supplied timing slice was 10 minutes for 2 completed items, averaging 5 minutes each. The slowest item was exp1270 arXiv Bundle v10 at 10 minutes, gated on exp1269 Paper-v6 Critical Fixes v2. The docs pass was effectively zero additional wall time. Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout with 4 MB allocated and 0% utilization, and gpu_monitor.py reported no GPU processes or warnings. Pre-flight checks were seconds-scale, not the bottleneck. The highest-leverage improvements for the next milestone are parallel CPU/GPU lanes, cached TeX/pre-flight paths, structured gate/compile timing, and batched docs reconciliation.

bottlenecks_identified: The closeout lane was gated by sequencing: exp1270 could not run until exp1269 critical paper fixes were complete.
GPU utilization was inefficient for the overall milestone posture. Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout, with 4 MB allocated and 0% utilization on each card.
No GPU zombie processes were detected. The process list was empty and the 4 MB allocations were negligible driver/context residue, not material leaked VRAM.
The scheduler remained passive with respect to idle GPU capacity. gpu_monitor.py produced useful suggestions, but those suggestions did not automatically launch or reprioritize DualGPU work.
Pre-flight was not the bottleneck in this slice: conductor rows for exp1269 and exp1270 showed 81 tests passing in 8.24s and 7.89s.
Doc reconciliation was efficient in this closeout slice because it reported 0 minutes, but recurring milestone history shows inline docs can become a critical-path bottleneck when not batched.
The arXiv bundle step mixed gate validation, TeX compilation, artifact packaging, and upload-status reporting in one operational slot, making the 10 minutes hard to attribute.
The operational telemetry did not split wall time into gate wait, pre-flight, compile, packaging, and docs components, limiting precision for the next retro.
improvements_suggested: Adopt a default parallel milestone schedule with separate paper/docs, CPU micro-task, and GPU lanes.
Use DualGPURunner automatically when both GPUs are idle and any queued task can run Qwen on GPU 0 and Gemma on GPU 1.
Promote gpu_monitor.py from passive reporting to scheduler input: idle GPUs should either trigger eligible GPU work or write an explicit no-GPU-work reason.
Keep TeX dependencies warm and cache the arXiv bundle build path so exp1270-style compiles do not spend time downloading fonts or repeated tooling state.
Split arXiv bundle telemetry into gate_wait_seconds, preflight_seconds, compile_seconds, package_seconds, and upload_blocker fields.
Batch docs reconciliation after terminal artifacts exist, and keep roadmap/changelog updates out of the experiment critical path when possible.
Preserve the focused pre-flight target that runs 81 tests in under 10 seconds; do not fall back to broad suite execution for paper/docs-only changes.
Emit structured blocked artifacts for upload-pending states so publication lanes are terminal even when an external browser/manual upload remains.
Add a next-milestone startup check that kills only material zombies under gpu_monitor.py thresholds and ignores harmless 4 MB residual allocations.
Record per-experiment GPU telemetry for every GPU-eligible task: first allocation timestamp, peak VRAM, average utilization, closeout utilization, and process list.
estimated_time_savings_rationale: A 30% saving is realistic for the next similar closeout: roughly 10-12% from running independent CPU/docs work while paper gates resolve, 8-10% from cached TeX/pre-flight paths, 5-8% from active GPU-lane scheduling instead of idle DualGPU capacity, and 3-5% from batched docs reconciliation plus structured timing fields.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Run a three-lane scheduler: paper/docs lane, CPU micro-task lane, and GPU/DualGPU lane.
Cache and instrument the arXiv bundle path so compile/package/upload blockers are measured separately.
Make gpu_monitor.py actionable by feeding idle/zombie state into dispatch decisions before the next task launches.

gpu_utilization.assessment: Inefficient from a throughput perspective. Both GPUs were idle at closeout, so the milestone was not compute-bound. If any GPU-eligible experiments were ready, they should have run concurrently via DualGPURunner.

zombie_process_assessment.basis: scripts/gpu_monitor.py --json reported an empty processes list and no warnings; each RTX 3090 held only 4 MB at 0% utilization.
zombie_process_assessment.note: There were no material zombie processes wasting GPU resources under gpu_monitor.py's >=1024 MB and idle-time criteria.

preflight_assessment: Not a bottleneck for the requested closeout slice. exp1269 passed 81 tests in 8.24s and exp1270 passed 81 tests in 7.89s, which is negligible relative to the 10-minute wall time.
doc_reconciliation_assessment: Efficient in this specific slice because the supplied docs item reported 0 minutes. The process should still remain batched/asynchronous because earlier milestones show serialized docs can dominate the slowest list.
parallelization_assessment: exp1270 itself was gated on exp1269 and therefore not parallelizable with its prerequisite. The docs pass, GPU monitoring, upload-blocker recording, and any independent CPU/GPU experiments could have run concurrently once terminal artifacts existed.

question_answers.which_experiments_took_longest_and_why: exp1270 took the longest at 10 minutes because it was the gated arXiv bundle step after exp1269 paper-critical fixes. It performed TeX compilation, PDF generation, tarball packaging, and upload-pending reporting. The only other supplied item, inline docs, reported 0 minutes.
question_answers.was_gpu_utilization_efficient: No. Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout with only 4 MB allocated and 0% utilization, so GPU capacity was not used in parallel.
question_answers.were_there_zombie_processes: No. gpu_monitor.py reported no GPU processes and no warnings; the 4 MB allocations are below the zombie threshold and not material waste.
question_answers.were_there_zombie_processes_wasting_reso: No. gpu_monitor.py reported no GPU processes and no warnings; the 4 MB allocations are below the zombie threshold and not material waste.
question_answers.could_any_experiments_have_been_parallel: Yes. The exp1269-to-exp1270 dependency was serial, but docs reconciliation, GPU health checks, upload-blocker recording, and independent CPU/GPU tasks could have run in parallel lanes.
question_answers.was_the_pre_flight_test_suite_a_bottlene: No. The relevant focused pre-flight checks were seconds-scale: 81 tests in 8.24s and 7.89s.
question_answers.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: For this slice, yes: the supplied docs item took 0 minutes. The broader process still needs batching because prior milestones repeatedly showed inline docs as a slowest-list item.
question_answers.what_tooling_would_speed_up_the_next_mil: GPU-aware parallel dispatch, DualGPURunner defaults, cached TeX/pre-flight state, structured timing fields, terminal blocked artifacts for upload-pending states, and batched changelog/roadmap reconciliation.

meta_reflection: The closeout was fast once the paper-critical gate was satisfied, but it still left obvious parallel capacity unused. The next milestone should treat idle GPUs and docs reconciliation as scheduling signals, not passive after-the-fact observations.
